basis: Peroneal peripheral nerve dysfunction causes paralysis; no primary skeletal muscle disease.
Renal agenesis defines the disorder; pulmonary hypoplasia with respiratory failure occurred in 1/1 assessed patient.
Severe polycystic kidney disease combined with defining TSC brain and skin lesions; pulmonary lymphangioleiomyomatosis is not common across all patients.
Immune-mediated microscopic inflammation of the colonic mucosa defines the disease.
Inherited isolated parathyroid hormone deficiency causes hypocalcemia; hypocalcemic seizures do not establish intrinsic neurologic damage.
Inherited melanin-synthesis disorder defined by skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.
Mesomelic skeletal shortening and Madelung deformity together with hereditary nephritis define the syndrome; immune causation is not established.
Intellectual disability, developmental delay and seizures define the disorder; dysmorphic features do not establish additional organ damage.
Plasma-cell/protein-folding disorder; cardiac dysfunction ~70%, renal injury ~60%. Frequent neuropathy, malabsorption and hepatic involvement omitted under the four-axis cap.
Bacterial infection directly affects the skin; postinfectious renal disease is a separate minority complication.
Larval tissue infection; neurologic abnormalities occur in 80-99%, muscle cyst occupation/abnormal morphology in 30-79%, often asymptomatic. Ocular involvement is <30%.
Lifelong inflammatory skin and bowel injury with immunodeficiency defines the syndrome; recurrent blepharitis, otitis and bronchiolitis are secondary infections.
Pituitary hormone deficiency and immunodeficiency define the syndrome; bronchiectasis and hair/nail abnormalities each occur in 30-79%. Recurrent otitis alone is excluded.
Multiple intestinal polyps define this umbrella; extraintestinal manifestations vary between subtypes and are not shared across most patients.
Inherited vitreoretinal disease causes retinal exudation, folds and detachment with reduced vision; retinal vascular abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Congenital cholesteatoma arises in and occupies the middle ear.
Genetically caused immune-mediated intestinal inflammation; no additional common direct organ injury is established.
The parotid is a salivary gland, included in the gastrointestinal axis; this umbrella does not imply infection or autoimmunity.
A form of miliaria involving cutaneous sweat ducts and glands.
Antibody deficiency with immune-complex renal injury and stage 5 kidney disease in 1/1 reported patient; autoimmune thrombocytopenia is a separate diagnosis.
Severe defective endochondral ossification defines the skeletal dysplasia; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 80-99% and causes lethal respiratory failure.
Hereditary endocrine tumor predisposition defined by pheochromocytoma/paraganglioma; predisposition alone does not establish damage to other organs.
Raised intracranial cerebrospinal fluid pressure defines a neurologic disorder; this is not systemic vascular hypertension. Permanent ocular injury is not universal.
Hydrocephalus and developmental impairment define the syndrome; choanal atresia/respiratory insufficiency and eye hypoplasia each occur in 80-99%. Hirsutism is non-damaging.
Bladder-localized ethanol fermentation defines an acquired metabolic disorder; microbial colonization alone does not establish an infectious disease.
